tasks.short: Confirm copyright ownership and obtain missing permissions for completed work.

steps.what: List contributors, borrowed material and existing permissions for the completed work.

loop.input: Completed work, contributor agreements and existing permission records.
loop.output: Draft rights inventory with document references and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; writer checks uncertain attribution and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or ambiguous documents go to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contributor terms and permissions often sit in free text with inconsistent wording.

steps.what: Determine ownership, missing permissions and whether any formal procedure is needed.
Prepare permission requests and supporting evidence using approved templates.
Send approved permission requests and follow up with rights holders.
Resolve permission conditions, fees and restrictions before accepting terms.
File permissions and record attribution, permitted uses and expiry dates.

tasks.design: Configure a rights register in the {CLM} or {DOCS}, linked to completed work and contributor agreements. A bounded extraction loop prepares the inventory, while deterministic templates and the {WORKFLOW} prepare requests, track replies and record approved permissions. The legal adviser determines the route, eliminates unnecessary applications and approves requests and commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rights evidence is scattered across documents and correspondence. Ownership and permitted use cannot be inferred safely from a completed manuscript.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and approval features cover much of the process. AI coding makes document assembly and record links cheaper; bounded extraction reduces manual reading.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed ownership, negotiated licences and territorial differences remain legal work. Copyright generally arises automatically for eligible original work; registration or other procedures depend on the relevant national rules and intended use.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising uncertain ownership, negotiating fair terms and accepting legal responsibility.

ambition.what: A searchable catalogue of material cleared for reuse, with usage restrictions.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time assembling evidence and chasing replies. With delegated authority, they can select already-cleared material within recorded limits; new legal commitments remain with the authorised approver.

reach.learn: Translate permission conditions into attribution instructions and publication checks.

evidence.claim: Rights inventories, template assembly and approval routing are feasible with document and workflow capabilities.
Copyright protection generally arises automatically for eligible original work; permissions and ownership still need checking.
The digest's text-and-data-mining provision does not establish permission to republish third-party material.

assumptions: The typical task concerns ownership evidence and permissions, rather than routine copyright registration.
The legal adviser may be internal or retained externally.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
GDPR applies to contributor and contact data. Access review is included; employee consultation depends on the change and national rules.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, publication territories and formal procedures apply.
Who owns employee-created and commissioned work under existing agreements.
Which roles may accept fees, licences or assignments.
Whether permission records are structured and accessible.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Which procedures can be removed because protection already exists?
Can existing agreement templates supply the required rights fields without model extraction?
What evidence must be retained for each permitted use?
new_work: Review uncertain contributor and permission extraction.
Maintain request templates, usage categories and approval limits.
Handle disputed ownership, unusual restrictions and unanswered requests.
Keep rights records aligned with later revisions and new publication uses.

tasks.short: Use advertising trends, consumer research and campaign results to recommend promotional approaches.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, promotional question and commercial constraints with the marketing manager.
Collect campaign results, survey reports and relevant advertising examples.
Align periods, audience definitions and campaign metrics in a comparison workbook.
Read survey findings and examples, recording themes, evidence and limitations.

loop.input: Selected survey reports and advertising examples with source dates and research questions.
loop.output: Evidence notes linking each theme to a passage, sample and stated limitation.
loop.check: Verify references and quoted figures; writer checks interpretation and contradictory evidence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per source; unresolved claims remain flagged and excluded from recommendations.
loop.why_not_simpler: Themes and limitations appear in varied prose and cannot be recovered through metric rules alone.

steps.what: Compare promotional options and write a recommendation with an explicit test hypothesis.
Agree the promotional approach, test limits and success criteria.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers approved exports from the {ADS}, {SOCIAL}, {BI} and {DOCS}, then calculates comparable metrics and flags mismatches. A bounded loop turns selected reports into cited evidence notes beside a {BI} comparison. The writer recommends a test, and the marketing manager approves its limits before campaign execution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports use different periods and audience definitions. Gathering evidence and rebuilding comparisons consumes time before interpretation starts.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic connectors and metric rules can handle repeatable preparation. Bounded reading can produce source-linked notes without pretending to establish causality.
tasks.still_hard: Survey bias, attribution gaps and changing audience behaviour limit conclusions. A persuasive pattern may still fail in a live campaign.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a commercially useful question and deciding which imperfect evidence deserves a test.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one message hypothesis for a limited campaign test.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more time interpreting evidence and proposing tests. If the marketing manager delegates a defined test allowance, the writer can choose message hypotheses within it; budget expansion remains a separate decision.

reach.task: Assess whether survey findings support a campaign hypothesis.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, comparable audience definitions and the difference between association and causal evidence.

reach.task: Translate a message hypothesis into a measurable campaign test.
reach.learn: Test design, attribution limits and stopping criteria.

evidence.claim: Coosto provides conversation and news monitoring, supporting configured collection of trend signals.
Archive question answering is being tested, supporting the feasibility of source-grounded research assistance.
Metric alignment and dashboard preparation can use deterministic transformations; promotional judgement remains context-dependent.

assumptions: The writer uses existing research and campaign data rather than commissioning a new survey in every case.
The comparison workbook bridges reports whose definitions are currently inconsistent.
Remaining recommendation time falls because evidence is prepared, while the decision remains human.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to consumer data; the design favours aggregate findings and approved access. Consultation under national rules is included where applicable.
unknowns: Which campaign and survey sources are licensed and accessible.
Whether audience and conversion definitions can be aligned.
Whether survey text includes personal or sensitive information.
Who may approve tests and what spending limits can be delegated.
Which employee consultation requirements apply to the implementation.
research_questions: Which research questions recur often enough to justify scheduled collection?
Which metric mismatches should block comparison instead of being normalised?
Can existing reporting configuration replace a custom dashboard?
new_work: Review source-linked findings and contradictory evidence.
Maintain metric definitions, source permissions and collection schedules.
Investigate missing data and changes in source formats.
Record test outcomes so later recommendations can use actual results.

tasks.short: Develop advertising campaign concepts and copy with creative, art and marketing leads.

steps.what: Discuss the campaign objective, audience, constraints and desired response.
Gather approved claims, previous campaigns, brand guidance and channel requirements.
Develop campaign concepts, narrative approaches and initial headline ideas.
Develop the strongest concept with the writer and art director.
Write channel versions and revise copy against creative feedback.

loop.input: Selected concept, approved claims, channel specifications and creative feedback.
loop.output: Channel copy drafts with claim references and tracked revisions.
loop.check: Run length, terminology and required-text checks; writer verifies claims, voice and creative fidelity.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision passes per channel; unresolved claims or weak copy return to the writer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting tone and narrative across channels requires writing beyond template substitution.

steps.what: Approve campaign copy, substantiated claims and the final creative package.
Send the approved package and production instructions to the delivery partner.

tasks.design: Use the {PROJECT} to connect each brief to approved claims, brand guidance and channel specifications in the {DOCS}. Deterministic assembly prepares the source pack, and a bounded drafting loop adapts the human-selected concept into channel copy with rule checks and claim references. Approval records lock the final version, and the {WORKFLOW} prepares the production handover for a recipient and version check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Creative context, approved facts and feedback are spread across briefs and document versions. Template automation alone cannot adapt a distinctive concept across channels.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding lowers the cost of source-pack assembly, version links and channel checks. Bounded drafting can assist adaptation after people settle the creative direction.
tasks.still_hard: Original concepts, visual and verbal coherence, stakeholder disagreement and judging likely audience response remain demanding. Faster copy production does not establish campaign effectiveness.
tasks.human_edge: Creating a distinctive idea, recognising cultural meaning and developing it through collaboration.

ambition.what: Channel-ready campaign packs for small regional marketing teams.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time collecting references and reformatting copy, leaving more time for concept development and art direction. They can accept routine channel adaptations within an agreed brief; campaign approval stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Develop visual treatments that reinforce the campaign concept.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, copy fit and how image choices change the meaning of a headline.

reach.task: Choose channels and define a campaign test.
reach.learn: Channel economics, production constraints and testable success criteria.

evidence.claim: A trial involving 444 professionals found faster completion and better assessed quality on professional writing tasks; it did not establish campaign effectiveness.
Acrolinx provides repeatable style scoring and quality gates, supporting rule-based checks around assisted drafting.
The digest treats creative writing as human work and bounded drafting as assistance for suitable writing stages.

assumptions: The company uses an internal creative team, an external agency or both.
Approved claims and channel specifications can be identified reliably.
The delivery partner receives production materials; publishing and media spending are separate tasks.
The proposed gain is concentrated in preparation and adaptation, despite the high whole-task gain prior.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to source material and audience data. EU AI Act obligations depend on the content and use; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether the campaign archive has usable tags and current approval status.
Who approves regulated or otherwise sensitive advertising claims.
How many channels and languages each campaign requires.
Whether external partners may receive drafts or only approved materials.
Which access restrictions and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which channel adaptations preserve enough structure for deterministic templates?
Which creative feedback can be expressed as repeatable checks?
What evidence is required before a claim can enter a source pack?
new_work: Review generated channel copy and its claim references.
Maintain current brand rules, channel limits and approved claims.
Resolve conflicting feedback and unsupported wording.
Check version locks and recipients before external handover.
Assess whether extra campaign variants improve outcomes enough to justify review.

tasks.short: Invent product names and slogans, then assess fit, language risks and legal clearance.

steps.what: Read the naming brief, product facts, audience needs and brand constraints.
Generate alternative product names and slogans across several creative directions.

loop.input: Naming criteria, approved product facts, brand terms and excluded names.
loop.output: A grouped longlist of names and slogans with short rationales.
loop.check: Check duplicates, length, excluded terms and unsupported product claims; writer reviews originality and fit.
loop.stop: Two batches of at most 25 candidates and one revision batch; writer continues manually if no direction is useful.
loop.why_not_simpler: Novel wording and associations cannot be produced adequately by fixed substitution rules.

steps.what: Develop and shortlist candidates for meaning, memorability, distinctiveness and audience fit.
Check shortlisted wording against existing names, excluded terms and format limits.
Check pronunciation, unintended meanings and cultural suitability in target languages.
Assess trademark conflicts and clearance needs using the {OTHER} trademark registry.
Approve the chosen name and slogan for the specified markets and uses.

tasks.design: A reusable naming form in the {WORKFLOW} assembles product facts and naming criteria from the {DOCS}. A bounded generator proposes candidates, while deterministic checks flag duplicates, excluded terms and format failures against the {DOCS} and {CMS}. The writer develops the shortlist, specialists assess language and legal risks, and the marketing manager approves a specific name and use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates can check constraints but offer little useful variety. Generating candidates has been mixed with the harder work of selecting and clearing them.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded generation can supply varied starting points cheaply. AI coding makes a small candidate record, repeatable constraint checks and a review pack economical.
tasks.still_hard: Memorable originality, cultural meaning and legal clearance remain uncertain. A registry search or absence of an exact match does not establish trademark availability.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a name people will remember, improving weak ideas and judging cultural and commercial consequences.

ambition.what: A naming review pack covering creative rationale, language risks and clearance status.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time producing an initial longlist and checking mechanical constraints. They take a stronger role in developing and explaining naming choices; legal clearance and final approval remain with the relevant roles.

reach.task: Assess a proposed name across target languages.
reach.learn: Pronunciation checks, local connotations and when native-market review is needed.

reach.task: Test shortlisted names and slogans on packaging and promotional layouts.
reach.learn: Visual word shape, reading distance and physical space constraints.

evidence.claim: Assisted professional writing has documented productivity benefits, but the trial does not establish naming originality or trademark safety.
Acrolinx demonstrates repeatable terminology and style checks that can support mechanical candidate screening.
Generating name candidates is feasible; selecting distinctive names and assessing legal conflicts require separate judgement.

assumptions: The workflow is for product names and slogans, rather than full brand strategy.
Language review applies to the intended markets; some cases require only one language.
Registry searches support specialist assessment and do not constitute automated clearance.
The near-total automation prior is too strong: candidate production changes substantially, while selection and clearance remain human.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
GDPR applies to any personal data in briefs. EU AI Act obligations depend on use; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which markets, languages and product categories require clearance.
Whether existing names and excluded terms are maintained centrally.
Who can approve a name and accept residual legal risk.
Whether confidential launch information may enter the approved model environment.
Whether access changes trigger consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which naming constraints can be enforced through existing document templates or forms?
Do generated candidates add useful diversity compared with the writer's current process?
What evidence must accompany a clearance recommendation for each target market?
new_work: Review generated candidates for derivative wording and unsupported claims.
Maintain existing-name lists, excluded terms and naming criteria.
Coordinate language and legal checks for shortlisted candidates.
Record approval scope and restrictions so later uses do not exceed clearance.
Remove weak candidate batches instead of expanding the review queue indefinitely.

role.altitude: The writer's week shifts from collecting references, assembling packs and making routine adaptations toward concepts, evidence interpretation and creative collaboration. Any new authority should be explicit: selecting cleared material and routine adaptations within agreed limits, with legal commitments, campaign spending and final naming approval retained by authorised roles.
reach: Market research analysts: turn evidence into testable message hypotheses.
Advertising and promotions managers: connect creative choices to channel tests and spending limits.
Graphic designers: develop coherent visual and verbal treatments.
Interpreters and translators: evaluate names and copy in target markets.
Editors: connect publication readiness to claims, permissions and version records.
skills_to_grow: Writing structured briefs and maintaining source-linked claims.
Distinguishing descriptive patterns from causal evidence.
Evaluating generated writing for originality, accuracy and audience fit.
Working with visual concepts and channel constraints.
Recognising rights, privacy and language issues that need specialist judgement.
Designing small tests and learning from their outcomes.
role.ambitious_version: A writer who leads evidence-informed creative development: bringing distinctive concepts, reusable cleared material and testable message choices to teams that previously received only finished copy.
